issue.title: Bound the runner-slot capacity scan and make the TUI GC policy cost-adaptive
issue.description: The sase TUI and waiting agent runners stop burning CPU and memory on full-archive capacity scans: a warm capacity scan costs milliseconds instead of 23 s, the TUI holds under 15% of one core and a bounded heap on athena, and full GC collections respect a duty-cycle bound.
issue.creation_reason: Approved epic plan plan:202611/capacity_scan_tui_runaway.md requests this work

issue.title: sase-core: capacity-only scan cost scales with live records, not archive size
issue.description: core-capacity-scan: in the linked sase-core repo, add a statx-only live-marker precheck plus meta-light closure classification (and, per the verdict_cache decision, a sticky never-live verdict cache) to the capacity_only scanner path, with parity tests and a scan-cost bench guarding identical retained records.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/capacity_scan_tui_runaway.md defines phase core-capacity-scan as one work unit

issue.title: Ratchet the core pin and re-measure the scan on the real archive
issue.description: sase-adopt-pin: move sase-core-revision.txt past the core commit, adopt any new scan option in runner_slots/_scan.py, and re-measure cold/warm capacity scans and runner-cache behavior on athena against the 22.9 s baseline.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/capacity_scan_tui_runaway.md defines phase sase-adopt-pin as one work unit

issue.title: TUI GC policy: full collections respect a duty-cycle bound
issue.description: gc-duty-cycle: record each full collection's duration in gc_policy.py and defer the next full collection by last-pause times a duty factor (clamped), applying the floor to idle and backstop triggers alike, with fake-clock unit tests.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/capacity_scan_tui_runaway.md defines phase gc-duty-cycle as one work unit

issue.title: Measured verification on athena and residual-leak attribution
issue.description: athena-soak: soak a TUI instance on athena for at least an hour under real agent load, verify CPU, rchar, RSS, GC-pause, and runner-CPU targets against the 2026-11-12 baseline, and attribute any residual RSS growth with the GC census.

payload.entry: Implemented GC duty-cycle bound in gc_policy.py: records each full collection pause and defers next full by last-pause times duty factor (clamped), applied to idle and backstop triggers. Focused GC policy tests: 37 passed. Full verification sase tool run check 1b260240f986521dbf1d2d9caf7fe43c succeeded exit 0 (verdict pass). epic-symbols clean.

Closeout evidence (the child epic close recorded this phase closed as delegated work landed at 05:24:46): completed Rust capacity projection, persisted v2 cache, parity and archive budget work is confirmed against plan:202611/capacity_scan_core.md. Repaired cache coverage for overlapping full/exact/filtered writers with per-worker legacy parity and valid pre-repair cache inspection, plus independent rejection of a valid cache whose root identity alone changed. Verified just fmt, all 15 capacity_cache_tests, and core sase tool run check 9b51ea06bb7129f25807eb397c094d27 (exit 0, succeeded); just symvision exited 0 with all public/private symbols used. Symvision rebuilt the linked core wheel; its LSP refresh logged sccache reset and temporary install-path errors but continued and completed. This is the already-triaged distinct sccache failure tracked as sase-1sp, not new scanner work. Both master tips refreshed with no drift (core bab59781, sase 4a4ee98c65), and epic-symbols audit was empty. Existing benchmark evidence at containing production revision bab59781: 20k rows, 175 retained, 27.84x cold improvement, 876.6ms warm, 40k warm 1679.6ms. Python pin/adoption and TUI soak remain with the outer epic. This turn's remaining core change is test-only and will be committed by the host finalizer.

sase-core-revision.txt ratcheted from 3416e4e24c84 to core HEAD bab5978195d9. RUNNER_SLOT_SCAN_OPTIONS already uses capacity_only=True and only_workflow_dirs=(ace-run,), so no Python option adoption was needed. Rebuilt the local dev wheel from sase-core bab59781 via just install-venv. Re-measured the real archive using a hard-linked copy to preserve the live shared cache: 190 retained records; cold scan wall 2.817s / CPU 2.513s; warm scan wall 0.9998s / CPU 0.998s, versus the 22.9s baseline. Warm narrowly meets <1s; cold is 8.1x faster, short of the >=10x target. The live ~/.sase/runner_slots.scan.json stayed 1,062,956 bytes with identical mtime over 12s while host runners were present; this observed a quiet interval, not a forced token bump. PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Investigate the real-archive cold capacity-scan result (2.82s, 8.1x vs the 22.9s baseline) and warm scan at the 1s threshold before claiming the stated scan budgets.

Pinned sase-core revision to bab5978195d9 and confirmed no Python option change was needed. On a hard-linked copy of the real archive: 190 records, cold 2.817s (8.1x vs 22.9s baseline), warm 0.9998s. Live runner scan cache remained unchanged over a quiet 12s observation. just check passed (ToolRun 6aba5705a062f0f46840126c04573aea, exit 0). Follow-up proposal records the shortfall against the >=10x cold target.
